title.narrative: Output 6.1. Increased capacity of Member States to promote investments in the care economy and a more balanced sharing of family responsibilities

description.narrative:
China Enterprise Confederation (CEC) developed the training manual of Diverse, Equal, and Inclusive Workplace in line with gender-related international labour Conventions. The training module 1 is “creating family-friendly workplace and help workers to balance family responsibilities’’.
In 2021 and 2022 CEC has delivered trainings reaching 200 enterprises and 2000 participants, and provided one-on-one technical guidance for five pilot enterprises. These enterprises successfully issued workplace policy on flexible working hours, improved supportive measures on breastfeeding, childcare, and protection for pregnant workers and new mothers. Two enterprises which have received the training improved their collective agreement to strengthen workplace measures balancing family responsibilities. Two companies introduced flexible working hours and established breastfeeding rooms, and one company improved its Code of Conduct for promoting family friendly working environment and introduced paternity leave and parental leave. ILO has strengthened its partnership with UN Women China to promote a family-friendly workplace. ILO supported UN Women to develop and launch its initiative on care work, by involving China Enterprise Confederation and national gender experts. ILO and UN Women jointly : a) supported the CEC in developing the training manual, carrying out a series of online and offline training; b) provided technical guidance and inputs to develop a questionnaire on the baseline survey and prepare the survey report; and c) assisted the CEC in selecting 5 pilot enterprises, reviewing workplace policies and measures, defining gaps, and one-on-one technical advisory services for improving family-friendly workplace policies and measures.

description.narrative:
In May 2023, the MOHRSS and the Supreme Court jointly issued the Typical Cases on Labour Disputes of New Forms of Employment (Typical Cases). The number of labour disputes over new types of employment has been rising with the fast expansion of the platform economy in recent years. The typical cases, as an interim legal guide, provide guidance to labour dispute arbitration bodies on how to assess whether there is an actual employment relationship between the different types of platform companies and the worker and hence contribute to strengthening the capacity of for labour disputes arbitration bodies in handling labour disputes of new forms of employment. ILO supported the Chinese Academy of Labour and Social Security of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MOHRSS) of China in conducting research on the Case Studies of Labour Disputes of New Forms of Employment in 2022. The team of this research are among the drafters of the Typical Cases. The findings of this research provided evidence which contributed to the preparation of the Typical Cases.
In July 2022, ILO supported MOHRSS in organizing a tripartite Seminar on Improving Labour Disputes Resolution Mechanism, at which the government, social partners, local labour disputes arbitration bodies, the Supreme Court and international experts shared some typical cases of resolution of labour disputes of new types of employment and made policy suggestions. The findings of the above-mentioned research were shared and commented by partners and other stakeholders.
